decision.explanation: The provided evidence from PMID 21796119 focuses on identifying somatic mutations in Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL), specifically discussing genes like MLL2, MEF2B, TP53, and others in the context of DLBCL and Follicular Lymphoma. The text does not mention breast adenocarcinoma, the EGFR L858R variant, or Erlotinib. Therefore, there is insufficient evidence to support, refute, or revise the claim regarding breast adenocarcinoma and EGFR L858R resistance to Erlotinib.

citations.quote: "e approach proposed by Greenman et al. We reasoned that this would reveal genes with strong selection signatures, and mutations in such genes would be good candidate cancer drivers. We identified 26 genes with significant evidence for positive selection (FDR 0.03, Methods), with either selective pressure for acquiring non-synonymous point mutations or truncating/nonsense mutations (Methods; Table 1; Supplementary Table S8). Included were known lymphoma oncogenes (BCL2, CD79B, CARD11, MYD88 and EZH2), all of which exhibited signatures indicative of selection for non-synonymous

insertions or deletions (indels). Three SNVs at splice sites were also detected, as were 10 new cSNVs that had not been detected by RNA-seq.\nThe somatic mutations were distributed across MLL2 (Figure 3A). 37% (n=29/78) of these were nonsense mutations, 46% (n=36/78) were indels that altered the reading frame, 8% (n=6/78) were point mutations at splice sites and 9% (n=7/78) were non-synonymous amino acid substitutions (Table 2).
